narr: A powerful winter storm, fueled by an atmospheric river, brought very heavy rainfall and significant flash flooding to parts of Southwestern California. The heaviest rainfall occurred across the mountains of Santa Barbara, Ventura and Los Angeles counties with totals ranging from 5 to 14 inches while coastal and valley areas in these three counties reported 2 to 8 inches of rainfall. Across San Luis Obispo county, 2 to 5 inches of rainfall was reported. Numerous reports of flash flooding and mud and debris flows were reported across Santa Barbara, Ventura and Los Angeles counties.

Significant flooding was reported along Highway 101 at the Castillo Street offramp. Vehicles were turning the wrong way to try to avoid the flooding. Eventually, both the onramp and offramp were closed.
Significant flooding was reported along Highway 101 at the Mission Street onramp and offramp. Hard closures were reported.

Significant flooding was reported in the city of Santa Barbara. Numerous reports of vehicles stuck in flooded roadways, requiring rescues.
Significant flooding resulted in the closures of Mountain Drive and Cold Springs Road.
